title: Invariant open neighbourhoods inside invariant intersections for affine flat descent
statement:
Let $p:X\to S$ be a flat surjective morphism of affine schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism]. Let $V\to X$ be a scheme, assume $V$ is quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], and give it a descent datum $\varphi:V\times_S X\xrightarrow{\sim}X\times_S V$ over $X/S$ [def-pd-descent-datum, def-pc-fibre-product]. For a subset $F\subset |V|$, write $F\times_S X$ for its inverse image under $V\times_S X\to V$ and $X\times_S F$ for its inverse image under $X\times_S V\to V$. Then for every $v\in V$ there exist an open subscheme $W\subset V$ and a subset $E\subset |V|$ such that $v\in W\subset E$, $E$ is an intersection of a nonempty set-indexed family of quasi-compact opens of $V$, and
$$\varphi(W\times_S X)=X\times_S W,\qquad \varphi(E\times_S X)=X\times_S E.$$
The first equality is an equality of open subschemes and the second an equality of subsets.

source.place: Tags 0APA (lemma-first-observation), 0APB (lemma-second-observation), together with lemma-constructing-invariant-opens; applied to the cartesian groupoid associated to a descent datum by lemma-cartesian-equivalent-descent-datum

proof.text: Write $a:V\to X$ for the structure morphism and put $R=V\times_S X$, $s=\operatorname{pr}_V:R\to V$, and $t=\operatorname{pr}_V\circ\varphi:R\to V$. The map $s$ is the base change of $p$ along $V\to S$; via $\varphi$, so is $t$. Since $X$ and $S$ are affine, [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine] makes $p$ affine. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](1),(3) and [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change] show that $s,t$ are affine, quasi-compact and flat. By [lem-galois-descent-datum-diagonal-identity], the pullback $\Delta^*\varphi:V\to V$ of $\varphi$ along the diagonal $\Delta:X\to X\times_S X$ is $\mathrm{id}_V$ (pulling the cocycle back along $X\to X\times_S X\times_S X$ gives $\alpha=\alpha\circ\alpha$ for this automorphism $\alpha$). Under the identifications of that node, $\varphi\circ(\mathrm{id}_V,a)=(a,\mathrm{id}_V)\circ\Delta^*\varphi$. Consequently the map $e:V\to R$ given by $(\mathrm{id}_V,a)$ satisfies $s e=t e=\mathrm{id}_V$.

source.place: Tag 0APF, lemma-cartesian-equivalent-descent-datum, specialized maps s and t; hypotheses of Tags 0APA and 0APB.

proof.text: For any subset $A\subset |V|$ put $\sigma(A)=t(s^{-1}(A))$. For each $z\in A$, [lem-pd-descent-orbit-saturated] applied to the transport defined by $\varphi$ gives $s^{-1}(O_z)=t^{-1}(O_z)$ for $O_z=t(s^{-1}(\{z\}))$. Since $\sigma(A)=\bigcup_{z\in A}O_z$ and inverse images commute with unions, $s^{-1}(\sigma(A))=t^{-1}(\sigma(A))$. Moreover $A\subset\sigma(A)$ by the identity section in step 1. These assertions also hold for $A=\varnothing$. Here the orbit lemma applies to precisely $R=V\times_S X$ and the target $t$ defined by universal transport, not to an unrelated action.

source.place: Tag 03LO, lemma-constructing-invariant-opens (1), using the existing singleton-orbit interface and unions.

proof.text: Choose an affine open $Q\subset V$ containing the prescribed point $v$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. It is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], and $s^{-1}(Q)$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-morphism-preimage-qc-open]. Hence $K=\sigma(Q)$ is quasi-compact: pull any open cover back along the continuous map $t$, choose a finite subcover of $s^{-1}(Q)$, and take its images. Also $K$ is closed under generalization. Indeed, if $y=t(r)\in K$ and $y'\leadsto y$, flatness of $t$ and [lem-weil-pbc-flat-generalizations-lift] give $r'\leadsto r$ with $t(r')=y'$. The open $s^{-1}(Q)$ contains $r'$ because it contains $r$, so $y'\in K$. Cover $K$ by affine opens of $V$ using the affine basis and take a finite subcover. Each affine open is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], so their finite union is a quasi-compact open $H\subset V$ containing $K$. In particular $Q\subset K\subset H$.

source.place: Tag 0APA, lemma-first-observation, quasi-compactness and generalization stability of the saturation; finite affine covering.

proof.text: Let $Z=|V|\setminus H$ and $T=\sigma(Z)$. Step 2 gives $Z\subset T$ and $s^{-1}(T)=t^{-1}(T)$. The subsets $K$ and $T$ are disjoint: if $y=t(r)$ were in both with $s(r)\in Z$, invariance of $K$ would give $s(r)\in K\subset H$, a contradiction. The subset $s^{-1}(Z)$ is closed. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-subset-closed-subscheme] choose a closed immersion $j:C\to R$ with exactly this image. The morphism $h=t\circ j:C\to V$ is affine: for each affine open $L\subset V$, $t^{-1}(L)$ is affine, and [def-weil-closed-immersion] makes $j^{-1}(t^{-1}(L))$ affine. This is the affine-morphism definition [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](3), $h$ is quasi-compact and its image is $T$. Therefore [lem-sc-picard-closure-specialization] gives, for every $y\in B=\overline T$, a point $y'\in T$ with $y'\leadsto y$. No constructibility or finite-presentation hypothesis on $T$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 0APB, lemma-second-observation, closed subset image; Tag 02JQ, morphisms-lemma-reach-points-scheme-theoretic-image (closure formulation).

proof.text: The closed subset $B$ is invariant. If $s(r)=y\in B$, choose $y'\in T$ with $y'\leadsto y$ by step 4. Flatness of $s$ and [lem-weil-pbc-flat-generalizations-lift] give $r'\leadsto r$ with $s(r')=y'$. Invariance of $T$ implies $t(r')\in T$, and continuity gives $t(r')\leadsto t(r)$, hence $t(r)\in B$. Conversely, starting with $t(r)\in B$, use the same specialization assertion and flatness of $t$ to lift a generalization into $t^{-1}(T)=s^{-1}(T)$; its image under $s$ specializes to $s(r)$, proving $s(r)\in B$. Thus $s^{-1}(B)=t^{-1}(B)$. Further, $K\cap B=\varnothing$: if $y\in K\cap B$, a generalization $y'\in T$ supplied by step 4 belongs to $K$ by step 3, contradicting $K\cap T=\varnothing$. Put $W=V\setminus B$. It is an invariant open with $v\in Q\subset K\subset W$, and $W\subset H$ since $Z\subset T\subset B$.

source.place: Tag 0APB, lemma-second-observation, closure invariance and the open complement; both inclusions written out.

proof.text: Now put $E=\sigma(H)$. It is invariant by step 2, and $W\subset H\subset E$. Since $H$ is quasi-compact open, [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-morphism-preimage-qc-open] makes $s^{-1}(H)$ quasi-compact, and pulling back an open cover shows that its continuous image $E$ is quasi-compact. If $y=t(r)\in E$ and $y'\leadsto y$, [lem-weil-pbc-flat-generalizations-lift] lifts $y'$ to $r'\leadsto r$; the open $s^{-1}(H)$ contains $r'$, hence $y'\in E$. Thus $E$ is closed under generalization. The affine basis [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis] and compactness give a finite union $H_2$ of affine opens of $V$ containing $E$. Each constituent is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], so this is a quasi-compact open; neither $W$ nor $E$ is asserted quasi-compact open.

source.place: Tag 0APA, lemma-first-observation, applied to H after the bounded invariant open of Tag 0APB.

proof.text: The open subscheme $H_2$ is quasi-separated. To check this without assuming that intersections of affines are affine, cover $H_2$ by affine opens of $V$ contained in $H_2$, using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. Their pairwise intersections are quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-separated-affine-cover-criterion](1) for the given quasi-separated scheme $V$. Clause (2) of that node applied to this cover of $H_2$ proves the assertion. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-scheme-spectral] makes $|H_2|$ spectral. The subset $E$ remains quasi-compact in $H_2$ and is closed under generalization there. Its set of generalizations is therefore itself, so [lem-weil-pbc-spectral-generalizations-of-quasi-compact] identifies $E$ with the intersection of all quasi-compact opens of $H_2$ containing $E$. This family is a set and nonempty, since it contains $H_2$. Each member is also open and quasi-compact in $V$: openness composes for open subspaces, and the induced topology on each member is the same. This gives the required nonempty set-indexed family of quasi-compact opens of $V$.

source.place: Tag 0APA, lemma-first-observation, spectral containing open; Tag 094L and Tag 0A31 (lemma-make-spectral-space).

proof.text: Finally $s^{-1}(F)=t^{-1}(F)$ is exactly $\varphi^{-1}(X\times_S F)=F\times_S X$ for any subset $F\subset |V|$, by the definitions of $s$ and $t$. Apply $\varphi$ to obtain the two asserted equalities for $F=W$ and $F=E$. For $W$ both inverse images are open subschemes, and equality of their underlying opens is equality of the induced open subschemes [def-weil-open-immersion]. For $E$ only subsets are used. Steps 5--7 provide $v\in W\subset E$ and the intersection description, so all clauses hold. If $V$ is empty the assertion quantified over $v$ is vacuous.

source.place: Tag 0APF and Tag 0APK, more-groupoids-lemma-ind-quasi-affine, translation to clauses (a),(b).

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NM-b9bc34ffd (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read all of the mathematics: the item, the parent's use of it, the statements of all 22 cited nodes, and the Stacks sources (groupoids.tex 03LO/0APA/0APB, more-groupoids.tex 0APK (a),(b), topology 0A31, morphisms 02JQ). The statement matches the 0APK translation exactly, with affine flat surjective p, V quasi-separated, v in W in E, W an open invariant subscheme, and E an intersection of a nonempty family of quasi-compact opens that is set-theoretically invariant. Nothing is weakened. Steps 2-8 are correct and follow 0APA/0APB. The proof writes out the generalization-stability of sigma(Q) and sigma(H), K disjoint from T, both directions of invariance of the closure of T, and K disjoint from that closure (0APB leaves this implicit). It sets W = V minus that closure, with Q in K in W in H in E = sigma(H), and gets the spectral intersection description on the quasi-compact, quasi-separated H2. I checked the edge cases: V empty, p = id, H = V, and V not quasi-compact. There are no new nodes and no duplicates (rg for 0APA/0APB/03LO/0APK and invariant/saturation wording). I accept the two declared tool_uses, orbit-saturated and spectral-generalizations. picard-closure-specialization is closed in Lean, so it is a tool. Fix (C5/C1): step 1 re-derived inline that the diagonal pullback of phi is the identity, which the existing Lean-closed node lem-galois-descent-datum-diagonal-identity states exactly.
